## How to participate in TidyTuesday

::: fragment
- TidyTuesday is a repo in GitHub
  1.  Every Monday a new dataset of information about variables
  2.  Load dataset in R-studio
  3.  See dataset and tables
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("tidytuesdayR")  # bare første gang
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(tidyverse)

data <- tt_load("2026-09-29")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
names(data)
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
df <- data[[1]]

glimpse(df)
summary(df)
```

Make for example a figure with ggplot, an analysis, model or Quarto
report, and share the result and your code on social media with the
#TidyTuesday hashtag

## Country music lyrics

::::::: columns
:::: {.column .incremental width="50%"}
::: fragment
Example analysis of a TidyTuesday dataset
:::

- Country music lyrics dataset

  1.  Includes lyrics, artists and producers
  2.  This analysis focus on producers
  3.  Lines connect producers and artists
  4.  Thicker lines means more songs together
  5.  Dan Huff: 59 songs, 17 artist (broadest network)
  6.  Some producers mainly work with one artist
  7.  Shows hos one dataset can answer different questions
::::

::: {.column .incremental width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"

library(tidyverse)

# resten av koden
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| out-width: "100%"

library(tidyverse)

# Load data
country_lyrics <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-08-25/country_lyrics.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Select producers
selected_producers <- c(
  "Michael Knox",
  "Jeff Stevens",
  "Byron Gallimore",
  "Ross Copperman",
  "Jay Joyce",
  "Dann Huff"
)

# Clean and summarise data
producer_data <- country_lyrics |>
  filter(!is.na(producer)) |>
  separate_longer_delim(producer, delim = ",") |>
  mutate(producer = str_squish(producer)) |>
  filter(producer %in% selected_producers) |>
  count(producer, artist, name = "number_of_songs") |>
  group_by(producer) |>
  arrange(desc(number_of_songs), artist, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    artist_position = row_number(),
    producer_position = (n() + 1) / 2
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Producer labels and totals
producer_summary <- producer_data |>
  group_by(producer) |>
  summarise(
    producer_position = first(producer_position),
    total_songs = sum(number_of_songs),
    number_of_artists = n_distinct(artist),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      producer, "\n",
      total_songs, " songs across ",
      number_of_artists, " artists"
    )
  )

# Create the figure
ggplot(producer_data) +
  geom_curve(
    aes(
      x = 0,
      y = producer_position,
      xend = 1,
      yend = artist_position,
      linewidth = number_of_songs
    ),
    curvature = 0.25,
    colour = "#70405D",
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = producer_summary,
    aes(x = 0, y = producer_position),
    size = 3,
    colour = "#70405D"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = 1, y = artist_position),
    size = 2,
    colour = "#70405D"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = producer_summary,
    aes(x = -0.05, y = producer_position, label = label),
    hjust = 1,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 1.05, y = artist_position, label = artist),
    hjust = 0,
    size = 2.7
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ producer, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_linewidth_continuous(
    range = c(0.3, 3),
    name = "Songs produced\ntogether"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-0.6, 1.6),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Some country producers stick with one artist",
    subtitle = "Others work across the genre",
    caption = "Source: TidyTuesday – Country Music Lyrics"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.margin = margin(20, 80, 20, 120)
  )
```
